text: For the choir director. Of David. To bring remembrance.

versions.text: For the choir director. Of David. A petition.
versions.explanation: לְהַזְכִּיר literally means 'to bring to remembrance' (possibly linked to the memorial portion of an offering). 'A petition' is an interpretive paraphrase that loses the sense of the Hebrew term; a footnote could note the alternative 'for the memorial offering.'

text: God, come and rescue me! LORD, hurry to my help!
Let those who seek my life be shamed and humiliated; let those who delight in my ruin be driven back in disgrace.
Let those who say, "Aha! Aha!" be turned back by their own shame.
But let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you; let those who love your salvation always say, "Let God be magnified!"

versions.text: But let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you; let those who love your salvation always say, "God is great!"
versions.explanation: יִגְדַּל is a jussive ('let God be magnified/exalted'), a wish or acclamation, not a simple statement of fact. 'God is great!' flattens the volitional force that parallels the other jussives in the psalm.

text: As for me, I am poor and needy — God, hurry to me! You are my help and my deliverer; LORD, do not delay.
